# Canonical-CID tie-breaking fixtures

`tie1.jsonld` and `tie2.jsonld` are byte-identical copies of the same-named
fixtures in `pflow-jl`'s `test/testdata/cid/` (`daf0a45`, merged to that
repo's `main`), which were themselves written during that port specifically
to exercise Hash N-Degree Quads' tie-breaking — URDNA2015's hardest case, and
the one a pflow net hits routinely: every arc sharing the same `weight`, or
every place sharing the same `capacity`/`initial`, produces first-degree-
identical blank nodes distinguishable only by which arc or place owns them.
`tie1.jsonld` is three arcs sharing `weight: [1]`; `tie2.jsonld` adds
`capacity`/`initial` on three places sharing the same values, tripling the
tied-group count.

Their golden CIDs (generated by go-pflow's `seal.SealJSONLD`, at the same
pflow-xyz commit `pflow-jl`'s copy was pinned to) are asserted directly in
`canonical_cid.rs`'s `tie_breaking_fixtures_match_go_pflow` test rather than
duplicated in a second `golden.json` here:

| file | sha256 | CID |
|---|---|---|
| `tie1.jsonld` | `7ef6aada73d84be35847769a55b66bc6a80272cb6b0e22e0e597a94546ab4240` | `z4EBG9jDqmAkYxzdaWnPVRZfBcpug1F45LeQJgck4MicFUDPFgS` |
| `tie2.jsonld` | `e13ea6966c1381ec033e683f6debdaa52c5b39aac4b5ed834fb927b45017a18e` | `z4EBG9j8AZSNguvWsF6uwoo9PWqURQV2f5YFiYfLXBb9SpvXgt8` |

`pflow-xyz/parity/fixtures/*.jsonld` + `parity/golden.json` are the *other*
half of the contract — read directly from a sibling `pflow-xyz` checkout by
`matches_pflow_xyz_golden_cids` (skips quietly without one) rather than
copied here, since a stale copy could silently drift from the real contract
in a way a live read cannot.
